title: Hot topic: why is Burnham so reluctant to talk about the climate crisis?

paragraphs.en: From the first day Andy Burnham came into office, climate scientists, campaigners and some of the ordinary people surviving through this summer of extreme heat began to wonder when he would start to talk about the climate crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 从安迪·伯纳姆上任的第一天起，气候科学家、活动人士以及一些在这酷热之夏挣扎求生的普通民众就开始疑惑，他何时才会开始谈论气候危机。

paragraphs.en: Up until this week, many held back from criticism. After all, he had only been in power for a couple weeks; it felt far too early to start to judge and call him out on it.
paragraphs.zh: 直到本周之前，许多人一直克制着不去批评。毕竟，他上台才不过几周；现在就对他进行评判和指责，似乎还为时过早。

paragraphs.en: But as we watched the footage of terrified horses galloping over cindering heathland in the New Forest while yet another wildfire took hold, it no longer felt too soon to wonder.
paragraphs.zh: 但当我们看到又一场山火蔓延、受惊的马匹在新森林燃烧的石楠荒地上狂奔的画面时，我们不再觉得发出疑问还为时过早。

paragraphs.en: Now people are asking aloud: why is Burnham ignoring what is in front of his face – the devastating impact of climate breakdown on the country and its citizens?
paragraphs.zh: 如今，人们开始公开质问：伯纳姆为何无视眼前的一切——气候崩溃对这个国家及其公民造成的毁灭性影响？

paragraphs.en: “As the prime minister tours every region of the UK, it will be hard to miss the impacts of this extraordinary summer: wildfires, drought, parched farmland and people struggling to work in extreme heat,” said Emma Howard Boyd, the former head of the Environment Agency who is now a professor in practice at the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment.
paragraphs.zh: 前环境署署长、现任格兰瑟姆气候变化与环境研究所实践教授的艾玛·霍华德·博伊德说：“随着首相巡视英国各地，他将很难忽视这个非凡夏季的影响：山火、干旱、干裂的农田，以及在极端高温下艰难工作的人们。”

paragraphs.en: She went on to call for Burnham’s government to “act with urgency” to prepare the country for a hotter climate, by cutting emissions while investing in the resilience of the country’s homes, infrastructure, farms and public services.
paragraphs.zh: 她接着呼吁伯纳姆政府“紧急采取行动”，为英国应对更炎热的气候做好准备——既要削减排放，又要投资增强该国住房、基础设施、农场和公共服务的韧性。

paragraphs.en: Mike Childs, the head of policy at Friends of the Earth, said it was time for Burnham to “end his silence on the climate emergency” and urgently tackle the causes and consequences of global heating to protect communities from increasingly frequent and extreme weather.
paragraphs.zh: 地球之友政策负责人迈克·蔡尔兹表示，伯纳姆是时候“结束他在气候紧急状况问题上的沉默”，紧急应对全球变暖的成因与后果，以保护社区免受日益频繁和极端的天气影响。

paragraphs.en: And yet Burnham seems to feel no urgency. There has been no speech utilising his trademark down-to-earth and compelling approach when it comes to the climate emergency.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，伯纳姆似乎并不感到紧迫。在气候紧急状况问题上，他始终没有发表过一场运用其标志性务实而动人的风格的演讲。
